newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAKS TO CHOOSE EITHER $250 MLN LOAN OR EUROBOND.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAKS TO CHOOSE EITHER $250 MLN LOAN OR EUROBOND.

text.p: Slovakia is expected to decide whether to launch a $250 million Eurobond or take an international loan of an equivalent sum next Tuesday, a senior finance ministry official said on Wednesday.

"The original plan was to draw a loan, where we could negotiate better repayment conditions, but it then changed to a Eurobond issue," Marian Horvath, head of the ministry's State Assets and Liabilities Department, told Reuters.
Horvath said the form of borrowing was still open and that more details would only be available after the government approves the final version at its regular session next Tuesday.
The government last Tuesday postponed discussion on the plan until next Tuesday but it gave no reason for the delay.
Horvath said that if the government approves a bond issue, the final sum could be higher than originally planned $250 million.

"Some 20 well known international banks were contacted and asked to submit their offers...and all of them have expressed interest. If the government opts for borowing through Eurobond, the final sum can be increased to, let's say, $300 million," Horvath said.

National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) Vice-governor Marian Jusko said last week that around one-third of the borrowed sum, either from credit or Eurobond, should be used to boost the basic capital of a planned Export-Import bank, expected to begin operations this summer.
The rest of the funds should help finance unspecified infrastructrure projects which were originally planned to be covered by the state budget.
